title: Brimming Tide
territory: A contained body of water becoming speech.
oneSentenceMeaning: A thought gathers like water, then takes the clear, familiar shape of speech.
appIdentity: Mluva is a small, capable place to turn speaking into useful text without breaking the rhythm of work. Its Czech name makes speech the centre of the identity; its Omarchy home gives that identity a practical, literate setting. The promise, ‘Most delightful dictation for Omarchy’, should feel plausible through immediate interaction, calm presentation and careful handling of what the person actually said. Original recognition, edited source and rewrites remain distinct, while Markdown makes the result something the person can continue shaping. Local and cloud providers are independent choices, so the identity should suggest personal agency without implying that every operation stays on the device. Brimming Tide expresses the moment before a thought becomes a sentence: there is already substance, and speaking gives it a usable form. ‘A little more delight every day’ belongs to that modest improvement in everyday flow.
markIdentity: The mark is one solid body with the familiar directional cue of speech and the upper contour of quiet water. A generous, rounded mass holds most of the visual weight. Its top gently dips and rises once, like a meniscus responding to breath; a short, broad tail grows from the lower right. These two decisions carry the meaning without interior symbols. The body is the thought gathered and retained, while the tail makes it addressed and expressible. Water also connects naturally to the existing film language and Omarchy’s fluid movement, but the sign must remain intelligible away from that film. At first glance it should register as a calm speech form; the water reading rewards a second look. The slight asymmetry supplies the organic quality Daniel likes in the existing breathing artwork. The geometry stays controlled enough for a launcher, panel or monochrome stamp, with neither a literal vessel nor an illustration of a wave.
logoDescription: Draw one closed, completely filled silhouette: a broad speech body with a gently tidal top edge and a small tail at the lower right. Its overall proportions are approximately 1.22 units wide to one unit tall, including the tail. The principal body is a softened, slightly horizontal oval whose lower half is full and settled. Its sides turn into the base with generous continuous curvature. Keep the greatest width near the vertical middle, and let the underside reach its lowest body point just left of centre, so the mass appears held rather than propelled. The contour must feel deliberately drawn, never mechanically wobbled. Across the upper edge, move from the rounded left shoulder into one shallow dip just right of centre, then rise into a broad right shoulder. This is one slow surface movement, not a sequence of ripples. The total vertical excursion of this meniscus should be about twelve percent of the body height: enough to survive reduction, but too restrained to resemble a breaking wave. The right shoulder merges directly into the side; it has no hook, pointed crest or projecting beak. A conventional speech tail begins in the lower right quarter. Give it a broad root, approximately eighteen percent of body width, and a short downward reach, approximately fourteen percent of body height. Its gently blunted tip leans right but stays within the body’s rightmost extent. A shallow concave return makes the tail legible without pinching the body into a neck. The tail must read as a speech pointer, not a water drop or separate appendage. Use a single, opaque ink fill, with no internal holes, divisions, outlines or floating parts. The water cue belongs entirely to the boundary of the same mass that signifies speech. On a 24 px canvas, the tail should retain roughly a two-pixel projection and the surface movement roughly two pixels of vertical difference. Optical adjustment at this size may broaden the tail root, but must preserve the same silhouette. Present the master alone on real transparency, with generous clear space. Its primary success test is speech recognition in a small monochrome silhouette; its secondary success is the quiet sensation of a thought brimming into words.
wordmarkDescription: Set the exact word ‘Mluva’ from JetBrains Mono Medium, then sculpt the resulting filled letter shapes as a restrained piece of brand artwork. The application’s editable type remains the unchanged JetBrains Mono family. Retain the capital M, lowercase l, u, v and double-storey a, the family’s characteristic construction, its upright stance and its measured technical rhythm. The word should still be recognisably related to a terminal, with a little of the tide mark’s ease. Keep every letter on one stable baseline and retain the original x-height and ascender relationship. Begin with the existing principle of a narrowed l. Reduce its advance and horizontal reach, preserving enough top and foot structure to distinguish it from an uppercase I or an isolated rule. Close the visual gap after M so the first two letters belong to one name; leave enough separation before u to keep the l’s foot out of the bowl. Adjust the remaining pairs optically, keeping u–v slightly more open than a purely numerical spacing system would suggest. The distinctive sculpting lives low in the word. Give the u’s bottom turn a subtly fuller exterior curve while keeping its inner counter open and structurally faithful to JetBrains Mono. Soften the v’s external apex by a tiny amount to balance its apparent weight with that bowl; preserve the unmistakable V geometry. Round only the most exposed outer corners by a radius no larger than one tenth of stem thickness. Leave the counters and major terminals crisp enough for small use. The a keeps its double-storey form and compact finish; do not turn its terminal into a wave, tail or decorative exit. All five letters remain separate. No ligature, watery cutout or fluctuating baseline is needed. Their shared lower weight and small optical corrections establish the relationship with the filled speech body. Produce one opaque monochrome wordmark on real transparency, without a symbol or descriptor. It should read instantly as Mluva before the viewer notices that the lettering has been tuned.

selfCritique.subject: Logo
selfCritique.initialDescription: The initial mark is a single pool of dark ink shaped into a low, organic speech vessel. Start with a broad, rounded body, about one and a half times wider than tall, with a substantial curved underside. Its top is a visible water surface rather than a straight rim: a shallow swell on the left runs into a central trough and then rises on the right. At that right edge, the wave lifts slightly above the main mass and curls inward before returning to the side of the body. The inward return creates a small crescent of transparent air that suggests the pressure of an imminent word. A short triangular speech tail descends from the lower left, balancing the elevated crest on the opposite side. The body, crest and tail are fused into one opaque form; no drawn outline or detached decoration is present. The design describes a thought that has accumulated and is just beginning to overflow into expression. Its visual energy runs from the heavy, settled base to the light, raised edge. The water should feel slow and tactile, with the soft continuity of the existing breathing artwork. Shape the left side more generously than the right, giving the mass an almost held-in-the-palm character. Keep the small crescent open to the outside, never enclosed as an eye or an interior counter. At large size, the uneven surface offers the recognisable fluid detail; at small size, the speech tail provides the category cue. Use only one flat ink colour, preserve a truly transparent background, and surround the isolated form with generous clear space. The ideal emotional reading is a reservoir of thought finding a voice: sufficient substance, easy release, no strain. The mark must work as a monochrome launcher symbol and as the still endpoint of a slow breathing animation. It should also sit over the film’s water footage without needing a new illustrative style.
adversarialCritique: The curled crest and opposing tail can read as a whale or a bird. The metaphor is asking viewers to decode too much before they reach speech.
The narrow transparent crescent is likely to close at 24 px, leaving an unexplained lump or accidental eye. It also recreates the old mark’s problem of depending on abstract negative space.
A body one and a half times wider than tall becomes too thin inside a square launcher allocation. The water character may survive while the speech cue loses weight.
Overflow implies leaking or losing information. That is a poor secondary association for a product that keeps original recognition separate from revisions.
A lifting crest promises drama. The product’s delight is quieter, and the existing film already supplies actual moving water.
selfCritique.decision: Revise once: remove the curling crest and crescent, compress the proportions, move the speech tail to the lower right, and contain the water cue within a broad meniscus across the top.

selfCritique.subject: Wordmark
selfCritique.initialDescription: The initial wordmark begins with the exact text Mluva in JetBrains Mono Medium and turns the lower half of the name into a restrained water rhythm. Preserve the capital M and the familiar lowercase sequence, but redraw the bottoms of u, v and a with a shared softness. The M remains the firm architectural opening. Narrow the l and tighten its approach to u so that the beginning of the name feels compact and intentional. Give u a deeper, fuller lower bowl, then round the bottom of v until its apex feels almost like the next small trough. Extend the a’s lower right terminal a little beyond its normal boundary and let it rise gently, echoing the mark’s lifted crest. The changes should be made to the filled glyph shapes, with no added decorative strokes. Keep the original JetBrains Mono x-height, ascender height and approximate stem weight. The normal monospaced advance may be loosened into optical spacing for the brand artwork, while all editable interface typography continues to use the actual family. Allow the u to sit just perceptibly below the common baseline, as round letters conventionally overshoot it, and let the extended a finish the word with a quiet upward motion. The intention is for the sequence uva to feel like three phases of one slow ripple without becoming a connected script. Retain an open u counter and the double-storey a. Use one flat, opaque ink colour and a genuine transparent background, with no separate logo or tagline. The result should combine the confidence of software typography with a small physical impression of water: grounded at the beginning, gently moving at the end.
adversarialCritique: The rippling uva sequence is too literal. It creates a second water illustration inside a word that should primarily name the product.
Deepening u and heavily rounding v can erase the family’s precise rhythm and make the letters look melted. That weakens the Omarchy and JetBrains Mono relationship.
An extended rising a terminal resembles a flourish or a smile. It can distract from the final letter and makes the name feel friendlier than the product’s calm, capable tone requires.
Tightening l toward u without protecting their silhouettes can make the pair read as a joined glyph at small size.
The proposed wave relies on a moving baseline. Even a slight visible bounce would make the lettering less stable beside the already asymmetric mark.
selfCritique.decision: Revise once: remove the terminal flourish and baseline movement, retain the source letter structures, and concentrate all softness in small exterior optical corrections to u and v.

revision.logo: The final description replaces the illustrative wave curl with one shallow meniscus and removes every internal void. Overall width narrows from roughly 1.5 to 1.22 times height. A broad, short speech tail moves to the lower right and remains inside the body’s rightmost extent, reducing animal and spilling associations. The body now holds its visual substance while the speech cue provides the meaning.
revision.wordmark: The final description preserves a common baseline, conventional double-storey a and separate letter shapes. It removes the a flourish, avoids a melted v, and limits curve changes to the lower exterior of u and a tiny optical easing of v. The narrowed l and optical pair spacing carry most of the customisation, preserving a clear JetBrains Mono lineage.
revision.status: One initial concept and one revision completed for the mark and wordmark. The final descriptions and production prompts specify the revised direction. This is a study; no production brand asset is changed.

logoPrompt: Create a single original flat vector-style brand symbol only, isolated on a REAL TRANSPARENT BACKGROUND with actual alpha. The symbol is a solid, calm speech form whose upper contour suggests a quiet water surface. One closed opaque black silhouette, approximately 1.22 times wider than tall including its tail. The main body is a generous slightly horizontal rounded oval with full sides and a settled curved underside. Across its top, one broad smooth meniscus dips shallowly just right of centre and rises into a broad rounded right shoulder; vertical excursion about twelve percent of body height. No wave curl or breaking crest: the shoulder merges directly into the side, with no projecting beak. A short, broad conventional speech tail grows from the lower right quarter, points gently downward and right, and ends within the body’s rightmost extent. Tail root about eighteen percent of body width; projection about fourteen percent of body height; softly blunted tip and a shallow concave return. The body, tidal surface and tail are one continuous filled mass, readable as speech at 24 px. Minimal, modern, warm through careful curvature, stable and capable. Flat solid black fill only. No strokes, outlines, interior holes, ripples, detached droplets, microphone, face, eye, bird, whale, arrow, container drawing, copied brand motif, app tile, background shape, gradient, glow, shadow, texture, 3D treatment or lighting. Generous transparent margins. LOGO ONLY: no letters, wordmark, labels, captions, taglines, mockups, sample applications, alternate versions or presentation board. Do not simulate transparency with white or a checkerboard; all pixels outside the silhouette must be transparent.
wordmarkPrompt: Create only the exact wordmark Mluva, capital M followed by lowercase l u v a, as one horizontal line of five separate filled letter shapes. REAL TRANSPARENT BACKGROUND with actual alpha. Base the lettering specifically on JetBrains Mono Medium: preserve its upright technical construction, capital M, recognisable lowercase l, open u, clear angular v and double-storey a. Tastefully sculpt the solid filled glyph shapes without changing to another font. Narrow the l’s advance and horizontal reach while retaining its identifying top and foot. Optically tighten M–l, protect the separation of l–u, and leave u–v enough air. One level baseline, original x-height and ascender relationship. Make the u’s exterior bottom turn only subtly fuller; soften the v’s outer apex by a tiny optical amount while keeping its V structure. Very small rounding only on exposed outer corners, radius no greater than one tenth of stem thickness. Keep counters clear and the a conventional. The effect is calm, precise software lettering with a little fluid ease. Flat opaque black fill only, clean crisp edges. No watery cutouts, wave flourish, connected script, ligatures, bouncing baseline, decorative terminal, strokes, outlines, gradients, glow, shadows, textures, 3D, icon, app tile or copied brand motif. EXACT WORDMARK ONLY: no other letters, labels, captions, tagline, font name, mockups, alternate versions or presentation board. Generous transparent margins. Do not simulate transparency with a white or checkerboard backdrop; all pixels outside the letters must be transparent.
smallSizeRisks: At 24 px, a meniscus shallower than about two rendered pixels may look like an ordinary speech bubble. Keep one visible dip and one rise without adding finer wave detail.
A narrow tail root can alias into a detached fleck. Preserve a broad connection and at least a roughly two-pixel projection beyond the body at the target size.
An exaggerated right shoulder can become a beak. It must turn directly into the flank and never extend beyond the main body’s width.
A long tail and a low body may read as an animal. Keep the final compact proportions and put the tail below the body rather than behind it.
The l foot can crowd u in the wordmark. Verify the name as Mluva at small text size; prefer a little more spacing over further letter modification.
Ink and reversed light fills may appear to have different weights. Any later reversal should use the same master first, with only evidence-led optical compensation.
opticalRules: Use one connected filled mark, one opaque colour and genuine transparent alpha outside it; no contour strokes or internal negative spaces.
Target an overall mark width-to-height ratio of 1.22:1, including the lower-right speech tail.
Limit the top to one shallow dip and one broad rise, with about twelve percent of body height between their extrema.
Keep the upper-right rise and the tail tip inside the body’s rightmost extent; neither becomes a projecting beak or arrow.
Keep the tail root near eighteen percent of body width and its downward reach near fourteen percent of body height; resolve those values optically at 24 px.
Centre the visible body optically, allowing for the lower-right tail’s pull; do not mechanically centre only the bounding rectangle.
Preserve a level wordmark baseline, JetBrains Mono Medium structure, separate glyphs, double-storey a and open counters.
Narrow l and adjust spacing before changing letter geometry; soften u and v only enough to equalise apparent weight.
Keep exposed-corner rounding below one tenth of the wordmark stem thickness and keep all fill opacity at one hundred percent.
Reserve at least one quarter of the mark’s body height as clear space on every side; use the symbol alone when a readable wordmark would not fit.
motionRelationship: The existing 3.4-second breathing cadence can animate only the meniscus and a small amount of body fullness. Keep the lower mass almost still while the upper dip shallows and the right shoulder rises by a small amount, then returns. The tail remains recognisable and attached throughout, and the silhouette never sheds a droplet, spills, curls into an animal or rotates. A maximum contour displacement of roughly three percent of body height should be enough in a larger recorder treatment; the 24 px launcher uses the static master. The motion expresses relaxed readiness, not provider progress, accuracy or guaranteed local processing. For a title reveal, let the final filled silhouette settle before the unchanged wordmark appears. The mark can share the film’s water background through shape and timing without acquiring ripples, reflections or gradients. Reduced motion uses the steady revised silhouette. The wordmark does not wobble or breathe; its stable baseline gives the organic mark a dependable counterpart.
